01 / A CLEARER PICTURELESS GUESSWORK. MORE GOOD WORK.

More than a star count.
A feel for the project.

A popular repository isn’t always the right place to start. CONTRI brings activity, conversations, and contribution openings into one considered view.

01

Is the project moving?

Recent human merges, contributor activity, releases, and repository context. Know what the data actually covers.

90-day activity · source-linked evidence
02

Are people responding?

Observed team activity, average and median first replies, and unanswered samples. Get context before committing your time.

issue opened··············team replied ↗
Human responses · honest sample sizes
03

Where can you help?

A badge under every issue title tells you whether it looks free, is assigned, was claimed in the comments — or the claim went quiet — or already has a pull request.

03 / FROM CURIOUS TO CONTRIBUTINGTHREE SMALL STEPS

You bring the curiosity.
We’ll bring the context.

01

Open a repository.

CONTRI recognizes the GitHub project you’re viewing. No copy-paste routine, no full-width dashboard.

02

Read the evidence.

See the overview first. Open Team for response patterns or Issues to inspect contribution opportunities.

03

Start a conversation.

Read the project’s guide and issue discussion. Check existing work. Then bring your idea to the community.

YOUR NEXT STEP, PREPARED

Bring your curiosity.
And your favorite AI.

01

Shortlist and watch.

Save promising projects and issues with private notes. Watch an issue and get a notification when it is unassigned, gets a pull request or goes quiet.

02

Summarize on your device.

Long thread? Chrome’s built-in AI summarizes it and suggests first steps — locally, without uploading anything.

03

Or bring your favorite AI.

Copy a source-linked contribution brief into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Nothing is sent automatically.

A FEW FIELD NOTES

Good questions.
Clear answers.

Is CONTRI free?+

Yes. The source is available under the MIT license. You can inspect it, improve it, and build on it.

Do I need to sign in?+

No. Anonymous mode works within GitHub’s limit of 60 requests an hour. Signing in with GitHub (read-only, no scopes) raises it to 5,000 and makes most checks a single request. Your sign-in is forgotten when the browser closes unless you choose otherwise, and it is only ever sent to GitHub.

How does it know who the maintainers are?+

From public evidence: GitHub’s team badges, who labels, assigns and merges, CODEOWNERS and the repository owner. That finds maintainers GitHub hides as “contributors”, but it is still not a complete roster, and every result explains its coverage.

Does “Looks free” mean nobody is working on it?+

Not quite. It means CONTRI found no assignee, no recent “I’d like to work on this” claim and no linked open pull request. Someone may still be working quietly, so say hello in the thread before you start.

What stays on my device?+

Cached public reports, your shortlist and notes, watched issues, preferences and, if you choose, your sign-in. AI summaries run on your device with Chrome’s built-in model. There is no analytics or backend. The full privacy policy is in the repository.

Is it on the Chrome Web Store?+

Not yet — the listing is being prepared. Until then, download the packaged release from GitHub and load it in a minute (steps below). It works in Chrome, Edge and Brave, with an experimental Firefox build.

YOUR NEXT CONTRIBUTION STARTS SOMEWHERE

Make it a
meaningful one.

Free and open source. Install it in a minute,
share feedback, or help build what comes next.

Download CONTRI ↗
  1. Download contri-v0.3.0.zip from the latest GitHub release and unzip it.
  2. Open chrome://extensions, turn on Developer mode, and choose Load unpacked.
  3. Select the unzipped folder. A welcome page opens — sign in with GitHub or continue anonymously.
  4. Open any public repository and look for the compass button and the badge under issue titles.

Chrome, Edge or Brave 124+. Prefer building from source? See the README.
